cold_open.hook: Iranian hackers took down LA transit for weeks—proving that critical infrastructure security has the same energy as a gym membership you keep forgetting to cancel.

markets.macro_note: Small caps outrunning mega-cap; oil bouncing on Iran retaliation fears; defense stocks quietly printing money.

big_story.story_title: Brent oil jumps back above $100 after Iran vows to retaliate for U.S. strikes
big_story.angle: Oil's whiplash from peace-deal hopes to retaliation threats exposes how thin the geopolitical risk premium actually is—and why betting on 'stability' in the Middle East is the financial equivalent of a house of cards in a wind tunnel.

quick_hits.angle: World's third-largest shipping line earnings crashed—global trade is slowing harder than consensus admits, and container rates are the canary in the coal mine nobody's watching.
Iran's internet coming back online after months-long blackout; the regime's digital stranglehold is loosening, but only because they ran out of ways to make it worse.
Ghost hackers—a cybersecurity mystery nobody's solved—suggests that the entire 'zero-trust architecture' industry is just expensive theater while actual bad guys operate in the shadows.
Elbit Systems leading defense gains on war demand; the market's already priced in a decade of Middle East instability, and it's not even hiding it.

odd_thing.joke_angle: Two people receive specialist care after TT crash—and nobody knows what TT is, which is either a motorcycle race or the world's most exclusive club.

yesterday_callback.topic: Oil prices tanked on Iran peace deal hopes—because nothing says 'geopolitical stability' like betting your portfolio on it
yesterday_callback.fresh_take: 24 hours later, oil's back above $100 on retaliation threats; the market's learned nothing and will repeat this exact cycle three more times before year-end.
